title: Python: ALIAS, a local with one binding to Cls.attr or mod.attr resolves as that attribute does (DEC-303 (a23) item 2)
description: DEC-303 (a23) item 2, verbatim: 'ALIAS is admitted. A local with exactly one binding, to Cls.attr or mod.attr, where that attribute resolves under the rules in force (A2, module attribute, Class.method), resolves as that attribute does. This is item 2 of (a22) (every binding enumerable from the scope's text, with the nonlocal proviso) composed with A2. Any second binding, or a right-hand side that does not itself resolve, stays unresolved.' Third in the (a23) build order after M1 and R4 (ALIAS, TS, Q1, (a25), NB-b, step 5) that releases the (a36) hold on the fresh blind sample. The call form is a bare call of the local (f = mod.func; f(), g = Cls.method; g(obj)). Lessons from K1, LIT, M1 and R4 to apply BEFORE the first push: enumerate every way the local gets a second binding with enumerableBindings (never S3 localNames), including a nonlocal write from a nested scope (read in the scope holding it: RawBinding.origin) and a comprehension target (not a nonlocal binding, RawBinding.comprehension); enumerate every way the RIGHT-HAND SIDE's own names get a second binding in EVERY module the resolution reads (the importing module, the defining module, a re-export hop: Cls, mod and the attribute), each with its own refused fixture asserting no edge leaves the call site and the receiver or name bin is unchanged; refuse module-level stars; read stars, globals, class bodies and annotations; every refusal fixture asserts the edge half (symbol ids) and the bin half. Report the five-pin per-site corpus diff, with every in-repo edge named, to the leader before the clear. Open follow-ups that touch this rule: GCLI-112 (PEP 695 type parameters bind no name).

acceptanceCriteria.text: a local with exactly ONE binding, a plain unannotated assignment whose right-hand side is Cls.attr or mod.attr (a dotted name of one segment after a name), where that right-hand side resolves under the rules in force (A2 module.Class.method, a module attribute, Class.method), resolves a bare call of the local as that attribute does, with red-before fixtures and positive and negative twins

each of these leaves the call unresolved, each with its own refused fixture asserting no edge leaves the call site (by symbol id) and the call stays in its current bin (bin delta against the same source with the call replaced): a second binding of the local by any form (rebind, augmented, for, with-as, except-as, walrus, comprehension target, match capture, import, def, class, tuple or star target, annotation, type alias, global declaration, a nonlocal write from a nested scope of any depth); an annotated binding; a right-hand side that does not itself resolve (a call, a literal, an unresolved or external attribute, a deeper chain, a name); a right-hand side whose Cls, mod or attribute name has a second binding in the importing module or in the module defining it (rebind, for, with-as, walrus, def, global write, star), or behind a re-export hop; a module-level star import; a class-body binding of the local

each rule has a mutation check that goes red (mutants listed by name, equivalent mutants said so), and a per-site corpus diff on the five pins is recorded, with every in-repo edge it creates or removes named per site and sent to the leader before the clear

implementationNotes:
Built (DEC-303 (a23) item 2, ALIAS). PROBE: before the change `f = m.func; f()` and `f = C.m; f(o)` were name-bin run-time-bound. BUILT in src/python/calls.ts: a new BindingRhs kind attr (the walker records `x = B.attr`, previously other) and resolveAliasCall, called from resolveBareCall after resolveInstanceCall. The local is found in a FUNCTION scope and has exactly ONE binding by enumerableBindings (a nonlocal write from a nested scope, a global declaration, a class-body binding of the name all refuse), an unannotated assign whose right-hand side is `B.attr` with B a name and ONE segment. B is read in the alias's own scope: (a) a CLASS by classSymbolOfName (one binding by item 2's enumeration, a class statement or a direct from-import of a module file whose own binding of it is one class), resolved by the A2 lookup methodLookup exactly as `C.m()` is, accepted only when it resolves in-repo (a method inherited from a base resolves; two defs of m resolve to both as C.m() does, multiply-bound); or (b) a MODULE bound by a plain `import` (not conditional, not a from-import of the module, so a package that re-exports the name is never read), whose attribute is bound exactly ONCE in that module file by enumerableBindings (def or class statement only: a rebind, for, with-as, walrus, global write, annotation, a star, an import of the name or a re-export hop refuses), resolved through moduleAttrToResolution as `m.func()` is (a class constructs). Anything else (external module, deeper chain, call, literal, name, missing attribute) is unresolved as before. Module-level aliases are not ALIAS (M1 and the plain-name alias rule are separate). FIXTURES (test/python-calls.test.ts, describe ALIAS, 5 tests): positives (module def, aliased import, module class, closure read, Cls.m, inherited, from-imported class, the plain-name alias unchanged); 18 second-binding forms; an annotated alias; nonlocal writes (rebind, another attribute, two levels, for target) and a comprehension target between the nonlocal write and the local (R4 round 1 class); global declaration, module-level name, class-body binding; 9 non-resolving right-hand sides plus a submodule chain, a class attribute, a non-def attribute; 11 importing-module forms (rebind, second import, for, with-as, walrus, global write from function and class, star, local rebind, conditional import, from-import of the module); 10 defining-module forms and a re-export hop, a package re-export, a hop whose re-exporting module rebinds the name, an external module; 17 Cls.attr forms (class twice, rebound, for, global write, star, rebound in the function, opaque base, m an attribute, m rebound in the class, no m, external class, source module rebind, twice, star, hop, package __init__). Every refusal asserts (a) no site on the call line (by symbol id of the app's line) and (b) the bin delta against the source with the call replaced: no more in-repo, no more external, exactly one more unresolved. Lesson caught by the mutation run: the first draft of the importing-module block omitted the m.py file, so the refusals passed vacuously; every such fixture now carries it. MUTANTS (replace-text, each run with bun test test/python-calls.test.ts -t ALIAS), 16 RED: hook-off, scope-kind, alias-count, alias-enumerable, alias-annotation, one-segment, class-inrepo, base-enumerable, base-count, import-kind, import-cond, defined-count, defined-enumerable, ctor-count, ctor-enumerable, rhs-attr-walker. Two first-draft mutants survived. The def-or-class kind test was REMOVED as redundant (only a def or class binding carries a symbolId). The `binding.origin ?? found.scope` mutant was WRONGLY called equivalent in the first draft and the origin was dropped; round 1 B1 restored it (see ROUND 1 FIXES): a `del f` in the enclosing function makes f a local without a recorded binding, so a nonlocal write CAN be the only recorded binding. The edge half of refused() was confirmed independently: with the bin half disabled, alias-count to < 1 goes RED on calleeId m.py:1:5. CORPUS DIFF on the five pins (flask 49943b5a, jinja 5ef70112, httpx 7cff5f79, rich 3a109ccd, tqdm 9cf5a12b), per-site multiset diff of bin, reason and edge list, origin/dev 0d74f61 vs this branch, script-asserted: every moved site is name-bin run-time-bound to resolved in-repo; total call counts unchanged; flask, jinja, httpx no change; no removal, no move to external, no receiver-bin move. IN-REPO EDGES CREATED (17): flask: no change jinja: no change httpx: no change rich (13 sites unresolved (receiver or name bin) to in-repo): rich/ansi.py: 183:37->rich/color.py:381:9, 187:37->rich/color.py:409:9, 199:43->rich/color.py:381:9, 204:37->rich/color.py:409:9; rich/columns.py: 80:13->rich/measure.py:79:9; rich/console.py: 300:19->rich/control.py:132:9; rich/markup.py: 163:34->rich/style.py:389:9, 222:39->rich/style.py:389:9; rich/measure.py: 145:9->rich/measure.py:79:9; rich/progress_bar.py: 113:47->rich/color.py:397:9; rich/table.py: 731:26->rich/measure.py:79:9; rich/text.py: 752:29->rich/style.py:601:9; rich/tree.py: 194:40->rich/measure.py:79:9 tqdm (4 sites unresolved (receiver or name bin) to in-repo): tqdm/std.py: 554:28->tqdm/std.py:368:9, 557:14->tqdm/std.py:368:9, 562:21->tqdm/std.py:368:9, 563:25->tqdm/std.py:368:9 TOTAL 17  Hand read: tqdm/std.py `format_sizeof = tqdm.format_sizeof` (a staticmethod of the module's one class tqdm, def at std.py:368) is the four ALIAS sites DEC-303 (a23) counted; rich Measurement.get (get_measurement, get_render_width, measure aliases), Control.move_to, Color.from_ansi and from_triplet, Style methods: each alias is bound once in its function to Class.method of a module-level class with one binding. Gap: `K = mod.Cls; K.m()` (an alias used as a receiver) is not built; the ruling and the AC name the bare call.
ROUND 1 FIXES (review of 11c8b5f0). B1: restored `binding.origin ?? found.scope` as the scope B is read in. The walker records no `del`, and `del f` makes f local to g in Python, so `def g(): def h(): nonlocal f; import other as m; f = m.func; h(); f(); del f` lands one recorded binding on g with origin h; reading `m` in g resolved the call to m.func though at run time f is other.func. Fixtures: the del input now resolves to other.py's func (not m.py's), and the writer-rebinds forms (`m = None` and `C = None` in h) refuse for the module and the class arm. The killing mutant holder-origin is RED. F2: the from-import-of-a-def fixture now carries m.py so it reaches classSymbolOfName (a def, not a class) and the classInfo branch; class-info mutant RED. F3: fixtures for a parameter then the alias, a sequence, keyword and as-pattern match capture, and a walrus inside a comprehension. F4: mutants: class-info (RED), path-null and base-kind SURVIVE AND ARE EQUIVALENT (type-narrowing guards: a non-name base has no .name so classSymbolOfName and enumerableBindings return null; moduleScopesByPath.get(null) is undefined, which returns null). F5: color.py targets are 381:9, 397:9 and 409:9 (Color.from_ansi, from_triplet and the third, named by line); each read. MUTANTS now 18 RED names: the 16 listed plus holder-origin and class-info (hook-off, scope-kind, alias-count, alias-enumerable, alias-annotation, holder-origin, class-info, one-segment, class-inrepo, base-enumerable, base-count, import-kind, import-cond, defined-count, defined-enumerable, ctor-count, ctor-enumerable, rhs-attr-walker); two equivalent, named above. CORPUS DIFF re-run against origin/dev 0d74f61: the same 17 sites (rich 13, tqdm 4), nothing else. F1 gaps shared with m.attr() and C.m() are named in the follow-up task: a package __init__ def shadowed by a submodule, Cls.attr = or setattr from outside, metaclass descriptors, a decorated class, an opaque base before an in-repo def, rule 44 type = m.func.

ROUND 2 FIXES (review of b3486a28). B1: the single-binding COUNT was also wrong under an unrecorded `del`: with two nonlocal writers the deeper one lands in the middle function (the nearest-function fallback runs before the other write is moved) and the other in g, so g holds exactly one recorded binding that is not the last one assigned. resolveAliasCall now refuses when the single binding carries `origin` (a binding moved here by `nonlocal`), which makes the holder-origin read moot (holder is found.scope again) and replaces the round 1 positive (the del input resolving to the other module) with a refusal. Fixtures: the del input with a writer importing another module; the writer-rebinds input; the two-writer input on the module arm AND the class arm (k writes D.m, h2 writes C.m, call after h()); a `global m` writer that imports another module. Mutant origin-refuse RED (replaces holder-origin, which no longer exists); class-info RED; path-null and base-kind remain equivalent type-narrowing guards. 18 mutants RED: hook-off, scope-kind, alias-count, alias-enumerable, alias-annotation, origin-refuse, class-info, one-segment, class-inrepo, base-enumerable, base-count, import-kind, import-cond, defined-count, defined-enumerable, ctor-count, ctor-enumerable, rhs-attr-walker. CORPUS DIFF re-run against origin/dev e13f2f8: the same 17 sites (rich 13, tqdm 4), nothing else; no site moved because its binding carries an origin.
